name: Okafor-Steinberg Evening Transmission
creator: Nadia Okafor-Steinberg, independent journalist
description: A twice-weekly long-form investigative news program distributed through gray-market neural feed subscriptions and physical data chips, the Evening Transmission built its reputation on the kind of corporate accountability journalism that licensed networks refuse to touch. Nadia Okafor-Steinberg, a former Axiom Network One correspondent who walked off-air in 2209 mid-broadcast, produces each episode alone from a mobile studio whose location has changed thirty-one times. Episodes run between forty minutes and three hours, with no advertisements and no corporate underwriting — funded entirely by subscriber Quanta and occasional anonymous drops.
medium: gray-market neural feed, physical data chip
cultural_impact: The Evening Transmission broke the story of HelixCorp's covert acquisition of Shelf water filtration infrastructure in 2212, triggering the only successful corponation legislative challenge in Meridian's decade — a story no licensed outlet would touch for eight months after.
controversy: Okafor-Steinberg was charged with three counts of Unauthorized Information Distribution in 2215; the charges were dropped after the source documents she cited were authenticated by two independent parties, creating an awkward precedent corporate legal teams are still contesting.
story_hooks: Okafor-Steinberg contacts a player character with a tip that requires physical infiltration to verify — she has the story but not the evidence, and she's being followed.
A powerful Tier 5 subject of an upcoming Evening Transmission episode is offering a very large sum to anyone who can identify Okafor-Steinberg's current studio location before the episode airs.
The Evening Transmission goes silent mid-episode during a live broadcast — the last audible words are a grid coordinate before the feed cuts.
